h1:
Where to stay in
Phuket Old Town
intro: Phuket Old Town is the historic heart of the island. Thalang, Dibuk, and Phang Nga roads and Soi Romanee are lined with century-old Sino-Portuguese shophouses painted in bright pastels, now home to cafes, local restaurants, galleries, and souvenir shops. On Sunday evenings Thalang Road closes for the Lard Yai walking street, and the whole strip fills with people. Most stays in the quarter are restored old buildings, from hostels and guesthouses up to boutique hotels that keep the original character. The big thing to know: this area is not on the coast. If your plan is to lie on a beach every day, the Old Town is not the right base, since the nearest beaches are a 30 to 45 minute drive away. But if you want to see the other side of Phuket, a real walkable town with great food and a lot of charm, it delivers. One more note: many old buildings have thin walls, so light sleepers should ask for a room away from the street.

blocks.html: Short answer: Phuket Old Town suits travellers who want to walk the pastel Sino-Portuguese streets, take photos, sit in cafes, and eat local food. It is not on a beach, so reaching the sand means a 30 to 45 minute drive. Stays run from hostels and guesthouses in old shophouses at a few hundred baht to boutique hotels restored from heritage buildings. Rooms start around ฿850 a night.

blocks.text: Recommended hotels in Phuket Old Town

items.name: Ai Phuket Hostel
items.meta: ★ 2-star · Best for: Backpackers · budget · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A popular hostel on Yaowarat Road in the centre of the Old Town, a few minutes' walk from Thalang Road and the Sunday walking street. It has mixed dorms, a women-only dorm, and private doubles, with an en-suite private room around ฿850 even in high season. Reviews praise the friendly staff, cleanliness, and the cafe downstairs. A good budget pick for staying right in the walkable heart of the quarter.

items.name: The Rommanee Classic Guesthouse
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Heritage guesthouse · budget couples · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small guesthouse on Soi Romanee, the prettiest photo lane in the Old Town. The building is a roughly 80-year-old Sino-Portuguese shophouse in pastel tones, with only about seven rooms. Standard rooms run around ฿890 to ฿1,000, with street-view rooms a little more. Reviews praise the location and cleanliness, and there's a free light breakfast. Note there is no lift and you'll catch some street noise. A good fit for couples who want to sleep in a genuine heritage building without spending much.

items.name: Sino Imperial Design Hotel
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Value · design rooms · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small design hotel on Phuket Road in the centre of the Old Town. Rooms have a modern mixed style, are roomier than a hostel, and come fully air-conditioned, with a light continental breakfast included. Reviews praise the easy walking access into the quarter and the value. A solid choice for a clean, good-looking private room at a mid-range price without paying full boutique rates.

items.name: The Memory at On On Hotel
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Oldest hotel · history lovers · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: The oldest hotel in Phuket, on Phang Nga Road in the centre of the Old Town. The Sino-Portuguese building has been renovated but keeps its original wood and detailing (it featured in the film The Beach). It has both dorms and private rooms. Reviews praise the walkable location near cafes and markets, the classic atmosphere, and helpful staff, plus free snacks and drinks left out for guests. A great pick for travellers who like a stay with a story.

items.name: WOO Gallery & Boutique Hotel
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Adults-only boutique · house museum · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: An adults-only boutique hotel in the heart of the Old Town, near Dibuk Road and the Chinpracha House museum. The decor reflects its Peranakan roots, and its standout feature is the connected heritage house museum, with historically furnished rooms and antiques to explore. Reviews praise the cleanliness, the spacious rooms, and the central location. A good fit for couples who want a quieter stay with character and no children around.

items.name: Casa Blanca Boutique Hotel
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Stylish boutique · rooftop pool · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A 4-star boutique hotel on Phuket Road in the centre of the Old Town with about 17 colourful, art-filled rooms. The highlights are a cafe with an indoor garden under a glass skylight and a rooftop pool. Rooms have air-con, hot water, a fridge, and a safe. Reviews single out the excellent staff and the beautiful, clean rooms. Worth knowing: as an old building the soundproofing is weak, and there's a bar nearby with live music until late, so light sleepers should request an interior room.

items.name: Hotel Verdigris
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Upscale boutique · private pools · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A small luxury boutique hotel with only about six rooms on Yaowarat Road in the heart of the Old Town, adults only. Each room has its own private pool and a free minibar, and there's a beautifully tiled central pool plus a reading gazebo over a koi pond. Reviews rate it very highly for the breakfast (sourced from shophouses in the quarter), the design, and the close attention to detail. It's the priciest stay in the area, and a great choice for couples who want a distinctive upscale base in the Old Town.

faq.q: Is it easy to reach the beach from Phuket Old Town?
faq.a: You'll need to drive. The Old Town is not on the coast: popular Patong Beach is about 14 km away, a 30 to 45 minute drive depending on traffic, and the southern beaches like Rawai and Nai Harn are a similar distance. The easiest options are a Grab ride or renting a car or motorbike. Local songthaews also run to Patong and other beaches from the town market, but they're slower and infrequent.

faq.q: Who is Phuket Old Town best for, and what is there to do?
faq.a: It suits people who enjoy exploring a town on foot, photographing the pastel heritage shophouses, sitting in cafes, and eating Phuket-style local food like Hokkien noodles, o-aew, and traditional sweets. There are house museums and galleries to wander, and on Sunday evenings the Lard Yai walking street takes over Thalang Road. Travellers who want to be on a beach every day or want Patong-style nightlife will find it quieter here.

faq.q: Are stays in the Old Town noisy and hard to sleep in?
faq.a: It depends on the room. Many places are old Sino-Portuguese buildings with weak soundproofing, and rooms facing Thalang Road or the main streets catch traffic noise, with some spots near bars that play live music late, especially on Friday and Saturday nights and on Sunday when the walking street runs. If you're a light sleeper, ask for an interior room or one off the main road when you book. Stays down small lanes or away from the main streets are quieter.
